laws.title: Meta bytes contract detects stale index past mtime lies
laws.claim: The build writes catalog_bytes and catalog_sha256 into meta so a stale index is detected by the recorded byte count even when mtimes are touched or a restore rewrites timestamps. The cheap per-search gate uses bytes plus mtime; the sha256 is the audit tier.

laws.title: bytes-plus-mtime freshness gate, hash as audit tier

laws.title: Build replaces atomically so ro readers never see partial index
laws.claim: build_index writes into catalog_fts.sqlite.tmp then os.replace()s it, so a crashed build never leaves a half index and a concurrent mode=ro reader keeps serving the old file. Deletes any pre-existing tmp before starting.

laws.title: Exit 2 is the fail-closed arm for every unverifiable byte
laws.claim: Missing carrier, unparseable **Tests:** line, unparseable date, future-dated census, and git failure all map to exit 2 via PatrolError or an explicit pre-check, so the gate never guesses a pass on missing or malformed evidence. Exit 2 is reserved for cannot-verify, exit 1 for verified-stale.

laws.title: Verdict cores are pure and fail-closed on unverifiable bytes
laws.claim: patrol(), collect_patrol(), and zero_collect_patrol() are pure functions returning verdict dicts; any cannot-verify condition (missing carrier, unparseable claim, future census date, git failure, pytest timeout) exits 2, never a guess and never a pass. The deep check also treats a None collected claim as UNVERIFIABLE exit 2.

laws.title: The census claim parses only from the parenthesized clause
laws.claim: CENSUS_CLAIM_RE reads counts and date only from the "N tests [collected] / M files (YYYY-MM-DD census" clause, so prose numbers elsewhere on the bullet cannot poison the parse; a non-canonical bullet returns None and exits 2 rather than guessing. The retired first-match regexes are named as the bug this closes.

laws.title: Prose numbers cannot poison the census parse
laws.claim: The census claim is read only from the parenthesized clause matched by CENSUS_CLAIM_RE, anchored on the "N tests [collected] / M files (YYYY-MM-DD census" shape. Earlier first-match regexes took the first date or count anywhere on the bullet, so tripwire prose like "31 files grown" ahead of the claim silently became the parse (B2-245).
